Criterion: tasks solved vs mean of 5 uncompressed runs (paired bootstrap 95% CI); cost ratios vs baseline. Model: DeepSeek-V4-Flash (self-hosted vLLM, temperature 0) for all. 84 evaluations (42 configs x 2 agents); grouped here, full values in Tables I-II. Table I rebuilt from jumbled pdftotext text, checked against text. - Baseline uncompressed + Mini-SWE-agent: 72.6 solved (71-76), 31.5 median turns; re-fetch 19/100 reads. - Baseline + Trae agent: 74.6 (74-76), 42.5 turns; re-fetch 9/100. - Delayed reasoning deletion (14 evals): solved -5 to +4, no significant loss; Mini 69-75, Trae 70-79; turns Mini -11% to +11%, Trae -15% to -3%; flat cost 0.74-1.05, caching cost 1.05-1.48. Quality works; cost partly (works flat, does not work caching-aware). - Delayed tool-output deletion (14 evals): Mini 69-73, Trae 67-74 (one significant loss: Trae token 75%, 67); turns +3% to +73%, 21 of 28 tool-output/both evals significantly longer; re-fetch up to 4.6x (Trae turn 100%); caching cost 1.03-1.70. Quality works; cost does not work. - Delayed both-scope deletion (14 evals): Mini 59-74, Trae 43-77; significant losses Mini turn 100% (59), Mini token 50% (66), Trae turn 100% (43), Trae token 75% (60); re-fetch up to 7.5x; caching cost up to 4.94 (Trae token 75%). Partly (<=75% turn-level) / does not work (100%, token 75%); cost does not work. - Immediate reasoning deletion (14 evals): 13 of 14 no significant loss; turns up to +105% (Mini turn 100%); no eval cheaper under either pricing; up to 4x cost (Mini turn 100%). Quality works; cost does not work. - Immediate tool-output deletion (14 evals): Mini 14-75, Trae 0-73 (Trae 0 at turn 100%, 5 at token 75%); runs up to cap. Does not work (except turn-level <=50% partly); cost does not work. - Immediate both-scope deletion (14 evals): Mini 2-72, Trae 0-74. Does not work beyond turn-level 25-50%; cost does not work. Overall: 19 of 42 immediate evaluations lose tasks significantly vs 5 of 42 delayed; caching-aware cost ratio >1 in all 42 delayed evaluations (26 significant)

Tasks: 100 SWE-bench Verified tasks (AgentDiet subset). Configurations: 42 deletion configurations x 2 agents (Mini-SWE-agent: single shell tool; Trae agent: file viewer, editor, shell). Baseline: 5 uncompressed runs per agent. Held constant: model DeepSeek-V4-Flash, temperature 0, high reasoning effort, ~262k context, 8,192 output tokens per call, default agent prompts and tools, 200-turn cap, Apptainer containers. Acceptance tests: hidden human-validated SWE-bench tests. Repetitions: 1 run per configuration/agent/task with one random deletion draw; 5 for baseline. Human intervention: none. Statistics: paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples) CIs; Holm correction as sensitivity analysis

Delayed deletion: 37 of 42 evaluations no significant loss in tasks solved; runs significantly longer in 21 (all deleting tool output). Immediate: 19 of 42 significant losses, 34 longer runs; immediate fewer tasks than delayed in 16 of 42 paired comparisons. Granularity: token-level longer runs than turn-level in 10 of 12 tool-output pairs. Re-fetch: tool-output deletion raises re-fetch up to 7.5x (delayed) and 10.6x (immediate); deleted outputs re-fetched 1.5-5x as often as kept (significant in 23 of 24). Cost (delayed): flat pricing cheaper in 26 of 42 (6 significant, 3 significantly more expensive); caching-aware none cheaper, 26 significantly more expensive; tokens billed at full input price 1.25 to ~10x baseline. Comparison with AgentDiet on Trae: 15 and 32 fewer tasks vs AgentDiet's 1 and 7 (design differences)

Distinguished timing, scope and granularity effects on effectiveness, run length, re-fetching and cost. Repeatability: temperature 0 but non-deterministic; single run and single deletion draw per configuration; CIs cover task sampling only; replication package with all runs. Limitations stated: multiple comparisons (Holm sensitivity: fewer significant, trends hold); scope confounded with number of tokens removed; data leakage possible; tests are a correctness proxy (patches not manually validated); caching cost model simplified (no cache-write premium, minimum prefix, expiry); re-fetch line-overlap measure (thresholds 50%/90% checked)

One open-weight model, two agents, 100-task subset (9,400 runs, >2,000 GPU hours); random deletion does not represent learned selection or summarization; infrequent rewriting not evaluated; settings (default prompts, 200-turn cap, two-turn delay) fixed. Implications: evaluate trajectory reduction on tasks solved, execution length, retrieval behaviour and caching-aware cost; token counts and flat pricing overstate savings. Future: longer retention delays, selection by observed reuse, less frequent rewriting, cost per task solved, memory management
